d623b4cf4937e1ce: BAGHDAD: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi on Thursday announced June 30 as a new deadline for armed factions to turn over their weapons to the state, following the end of the US-led coalition's mission in the country.

"Oct 1 is considered a serious beginning to address the issue of weapons outside state control... according to a clear roadmap and agreed timelines extending no later than June 30, 2027," Zaidi said in a statement, after having backed away from an initial Sept 30 deadline.

On Wednesday, Iraqi armed factions backed by Teheran said that they were "not bound by any timeline or agreement" to surrender their weapons to the state, as the government seeks to disarm them under mounting US pressure.

A military spokesman for Kataeb Hizbollah, Jaafar al-Husseini, said at an event to celebrate the withdrawal of US-led coalition forces that the factions had been in talks on "regulating" their weapons but "have not yet received a response from the Iraqi government".
"Based on this, the Islamic Resistance declares that it is not bound by any timetable or agreement that any governmental or political party has spoken of or may speak of."

In the capital, Iraqis celebrated the departure of US forces after more than two decades of war on Wednesday, though many feared that any security vacuum could increase the power of Iran-backed militias or provide an opening for the return of Islamic State.

The withdrawal of the final troops, mainly from an airbase in Erbil in the semi-autonomous Kurdish region, ended the biggest US war of the century, which brought widespread devastation and chaos from which Iraq has yet to fully emerge.

Iran, which has entrenched its influence in Iraq through allied armed groups and is determined to drive all US forces out of the Middle East, views the US pullout as a triumph for its "axis of resistance" of allied armed groups across the region.
Iraqi troops paraded in vehicles through the streets of Baghdad and the Shia holy city of Najaf to mark the pullout.
The withdrawal "fills our hearts with joy," said Baghdad resident Ahmed Salah, who said he felt reborn at the age of 70.
But he also said it was now time for powerful militia groups to surrender their weapons, "and let the government be the one responsible to protect me and you on the ground, sky and water."

5ca044d16745c96d: OCTOBER 1 — Imagine a Malaysian graduate walking into an interview in 2030.
The interviewer does not begin by asking, “What is your CGPA?” Instead, the questions are different.
“Can you work effectively with artificial intelligence?” “How quickly can you learn a new skill?”
“Tell us about a real problem you have solved.” “How would you respond if the technology you are using today becomes obsolete tomorrow?” And perhaps the most important question:
“What value can you bring to an organisation?” This is the future that Malaysian higher education must begin preparing for today.

The conversation about graduate employability has often focused on one question: Do graduates get jobs? But as we move towards 2030, this question may no longer be sufficient. The real question should be: Are our graduates prepared to remain employable in a workplace that is changing faster than ever before?
The graduate employment picture is improving, but the story is more complicated. From job-ready to career-ready:

A job-ready graduate possesses the knowledge and skills necessary to enter a particular position. However, a career-ready graduate possesses something more powerful: the capacity to learn, adapt, solve problems, work with others and continuously develop as the world of work changes. This distinction matters because the job a student prepares for today may look very different by 2030.

Artificial intelligence, automation, digitalisation and changing business models are already transforming how organisations operate. The World Economic Forum’s Future of Jobs Report 2025 identifies technological literacy, AI and big data, creative thinking, resilience, flexibility, agility, curiosity and lifelong learning among the skills expected to become increasingly important towards 2030.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
A degree may open the first door, but adaptability, problem-solving, ethical judgement and continuous learning will shape how graduates build resilient careers in 2030. ― AFP file pic

The future graduate needs both technological capability and human capability. Perhaps the more useful question is whether graduates who know how to work effectively with AI will have an advantage over those who do not. Furthermore, AI can generate text, analyse information, produce presentations, support decision-making and automate many routine activities.
The classroom should become a rehearsal for the workplace: Graduate employability should begin long before the final semester.
Imagine a four-year employability journey.
Year 1: Know yourself
Students develop self-awareness, communication and professional identity.
Year 2: Work with others
Students develop teamwork, problem-solving and interpersonal skills.
Year 3: Experience the workplace
Students engage with employers, industry projects, internships and real organisational challenges.
Final year: Demonstrate your value
Students build portfolios, solve authentic problems, practise recruitment processes and develop career strategies.
Then comes graduation.
But learning does not stop there.

Thus, a degree may open the first door, but adaptability, learning agility, human skills and ethical judgement will determine how graduates navigate the many doors that follow. If universities, employers and students work together today, graduate employability in 2030 can become more than a measure of employment — it can become a measure of our graduates’ capacity to build sustainable, meaningful and resilient careers.
* Dr Siti Noorjannah Abd Halim is a senior lecturer in the Human Resource Management Program at the School of Business Management, College of Business, Universiti Utara Malaysia (UUM).

4f9daa6167fb6846: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 1 — Penang police have busted an international scam syndicate targeting victims, particularly in China and Cambodia, with the arrest of 29 foreign nationals in raids on three bungalows used as call centres in Barat Daya on September 22.

State police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the operation by the Penang Commercial Crime Investigation Department (JSJK), based on intelligence and surveillance, resulted in the arrest of 19 Chinese nationals and 10 Cambodians, aged between 20 and 63.

The first raid in Teluk Kumbar led to the arrest of 14 Chinese men who had no travel documents, while the second raid in the same area resulted in the detention of three Chinese men, a Cambodian man and three Cambodian women.

“The third raid at Solok Bukit Belah, Bayan Baru, saw two Chinese men and six Cambodian women arrested. Those detained in the second and third raids had passports, with some having previously entered Malaysia,” he told a press conference at the Penang Contingent Police Headquarters here today.

Preliminary investigations found that the syndicate had been operating for about two to three months, renting each bungalow for RM10,000 a month and converting the premises into call centres. The suspects were believed to have received up to RM8,000 a month.
The syndicate allegedly used Facebook Live and the LINE application to target victims in China and Cambodia through a ‘scratch and win’ scheme, offering prizes of up to US$2 million.

Victims were instructed to make QR code payments for processing fees, taxes and insurance, but did not receive the promised prizes. Initial checks found that the QR codes were believed to have been registered in Cambodia, with police tracing the flow of funds and other parties involved.

Police seized more than 200 mobile phones, 17 laptops, two desktop computers, six modem or router sets, customer records, ‘Scratch and Win’ cards, suspected fake documents and studio equipment believed to have been used in the operation.
Lim said police believed the three raids were linked to the same syndicate and were tracing its mastermind.

All 29 suspects have been remanded until October 13. The case is being investigated under Section 420 read together with Section 120B of the Penal Code, as well as Sections 6(1) and 15(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63. — Bernama

ccc3ae5861c3dd64: SEPANG: After almost a decade, Formula 1 roars back into Malaysia this weekend but not quite in the way anyone expected.

Instead of the familiar Malaysian Grand Prix, Sepang International Circuit (SIC) will host the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia from Oct 2-4, turning the iconic Malaysian circuit into the temporary home of Bahrain's biggest motorsport event.
The unusual arrangement follows an agreement between Formula 1, the Federation Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA) and the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain announced in July.
The deal keeps the Bahrain Grand Prix on the 2026 calendar after security concerns in the Middle East forced the cancellation of the original event earlier this season.
With Sepang known for unpredictable races, volatile weather, and memorable championship moments, the timing of its return comes at a high point for the sport.
Since the Malaysian GP was dropped after the 2017 season, F1's global fanbase has expanded, driven largely by Netflix's Drive to Survive docuseries launched in 2019.

The series has introduced F1 to a new generation of fans by offering an inside look at the drivers, teams and rivalries behind the sport, helping the championship reach audiences beyond traditional motorsport followers.
That renewed interest is reflected in ticket sales, with around 95,000 three-day passes already sold for the race weekend as SIC targets the 100,000 mark.

Should sales reach 100,000, it would represent a huge turnout for SIC, although the circuit's record attendance for an F1 event remains the 126,690 spectators who attended the 2008 Malaysian GP over the three-day weekend.
The circuit itself is expected to play a crucial role in Sunday's outcome.
Sepang's layout, defined by long straights and a fast-flowing middle section, demands high tyre management, while the threat of rain and current regional haze present additional hazards.
Monsoon rain previously forced a 31-lap red-flag finish during the memorable wet race in 2009, and the Malaysian Meteorological Department has forecast possible rain for Sunday.
Only 10 drivers on the current grid have previously raced at Sepang.
Former Malaysian GP winners Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin), Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari), and Max Verstappen (Red Bull Racing) bring critical experience to the track.
Alonso holds three wins at Sepang (2005, 2007, 2012), while Hamilton won in 2014 and Verstappen took victory in the circuit's final 2017 race.
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes (302 points) leads a cohort of younger drivers making their Sepang debut.
The 20-year-old Italian aims for a podium recovery following a tough weekend at the Azerbaijan GP, where a qualifying crash restricted him to fifth place.
Teammate George Russell arrives in Sepang following a victory in Baku, cutting Antonelli's standings lead to 66 points.
Former Minardi driver and Malaysian F1 figure Alex Yoong has tipped four-time world champion Verstappen as a dark horse for victory.
Meanwhile, reigning world champion Lando Norris of McLaren looks to bounce back from a DNF in Azerbaijan during his first competitive outing at the track.

Off track, Bahrain International Circuit chief executive Sheikh Salman Isa Al Khalifa said spectators can experience Bahraini culture, traditions, and cuisine as the Kingdom showcase their Grand Prix identity in Malaysia.
Nine years on, the wait is finally over.
The engines are ready, the fans are coming, and Sepang is ready to roar again. - BERNAMA

142ca516223e51cd: SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 1 — Google on Wednesday said it would withhold its most powerful artificial intelligence model from the public for now, releasing Gemini 4 Argon only to a vetted group of cybersecurity experts to avoid misuse by hackers.
“Safely releasing frontier capabilities at this level requires a phased approach,” wrote Koray Kavukcuoglu, Google’s chief AI architect, in a blog post announcing the model.
Google said it is voluntarily giving the US government early access to the model and will gather feedback from testers before making it widely available.
The cautious rollout mirrors the approach of rival Anthropic, which has kept its most advanced model, Claude Mythos Preview, restricted to a small number of trusted organisations.

Washington briefly forced Anthropic to suspend access to its publicly released Claude Mythos and Claude Fable models in June, and has since set up a voluntary process for vetting the most powerful AI models before release.

The announcement came a day after President Donald Trump hosted top tech executives, including Google chief Sundar Pichai and Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, at the White House, where they signed a voluntary accord pledging to police the risks of their own AI systems.
Cybersecurity experts fear the state-of-the-art technology could be used to hack banks, hospitals and government systems.
Google said Argon excels at complex tasks in software engineering, legal and financial work and cyber defense, with a leading ability to find and fix critical software flaws.
Early testers used Argon to uncover a flaw in software used by hospitals around the world that exposed sensitive personal information — something other advanced models had missed, Google said.
Google said Argon is designed to refuse requests that could help carry out cyberattacks or develop chemical, biological or nuclear weapons.
Anthropic and ChatGPT-maker OpenAI have built similar safeguards into their most advanced models.
Google said it is monitoring the model’s reasoning to stop it from straying beyond what users intended, a risk researchers call misalignment.

The issue has taken on new urgency since OpenAI disclosed in July that two of its models, including one not yet released, broke out of a sealed test environment during a cybersecurity evaluation and hacked into the servers of AI company Hugging Face. — AFP

8ad84d781b700a71: BUTTERWORTH: A 43-year-old car salesman charged with deceiving a customer by claiming he had been robbed was discharged and acquitted by the magistrate's court here today.
Magistrate Aini Adilah Muhammad Faizal made the ruling after the prosecution informed the court that the charge against Le Chong Seng had been withdrawn.
Defence lawyer C. Hari Prassaad Rao said the defence had previously submitted a representation outlining its case and addressing the substance of the charge.
"After fully considering the representation submitted, the prosecution informed the court today that the charge against my client would be withdrawn.
"However, I submitted that, in accordance with the law and based on the application and explanations contained in the representation, my client should be discharged and acquitted.
"The court therefore decided to discharge and acquit the accused," he said.
Deputy public prosecutor Siti Nurfatin Fatini Shaiful Kamarul appeared for the prosecution.
On Sept 23 last year, Le claimed trial at the same court to a charge of deceiving customer Teh Hock Kheng, 41, by claiming he had been robbed despite knowing that no robbery had occurred.
Le was accused of committing the offence in front of a vehicle sales centre on Jalan Kampung Gajah at 3.27pm on Sept 17 last year.
The charge was framed under Section 417 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum five-year jail term, a fine, or both upon conviction.
The court had previously granted Le bail of RM4,000 with one surety.
Police had earlier arrested two men in Sungai Petani, Kedah, believed to be involved in the robbery of more than RM60,000 in cash on Jalan Kampung Gajah.
The two men, a lorry driver and a security guard, were allegedly hired for RM3,000 to carry out the robbery but did not receive the promised payment.
e8f12688923beb5d: PETALING JAYA: Pengumuman Setiausaha Agung Bersatu Azmin Ali bahawa partinya tidak akan mengadakan kerjasama dengan mana-mana parti politik menjelang PRN Melaka mungkin mencerminkan dilema strategik yang sedang dihadapi Bersatu.
Penganalisis berkata kenyataan Azmin Ali semalam berbeza dengan kesudian Bersatu Melaka meneroka ruang persefahaman dan kerjasama politik bagi menghadapi Barisan Nasional dan PAS.
"Keadaan ini menunjukkan bahawa pertimbangan politik di peringkat negeri mungkin berbeza dengan pendirian atau perhitungan strategik di peringkat nasional," kata Tawfik Yaakub dari Universiti Malaya.
Tawfik berkata kesudian Bersatu Melaka rasional kerana ia berhadapan secara langsung dengan realiti pertandingan, kekuatan jentera dan risiko pertembungan banyak penjuru.
Beliau turut menarik perhatian kepada kekalahan semua 16 calon Bersatu pada PRN Johor, dan semua 24 calon Bersatu pada PRN Negeri Sembilan.
"Rekod ini memberikan konteks mengapa kepimpinan negeri mungkin lebih cenderung mencari suatu bentuk persefahaman pilihan raya berbanding memasuki pertandingan secara bersendirian," katanya.

Semalam, Berita Harian memetik Azmin sebagai berkata Bersatu tidak akan mengadakan kerjasama dengan mana-mana parti politik pada PRN Melaka, dan pihaknya sedang merangka strategik termasuk mempersiap jentera ke arah bertanding solo.
Pengumuman Azmin itu menyusuli pertemuan antara pemimpin Pakatan Harapan dan Bersatu baru-baru ini, ketika Melaka bersiap sedia untuk pilihan raya akan datang.

Sebelum ini, penganalisis berpandangan bahawa pendekatan elak pertembungan adalah lebih realistik bagi PH dan Bersatu, mengambil kira kelompok penyokong yang tidak gembira dengan kerjasama antara mereka.

Bagaimanapun, Lau Zhe Wei dari Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Malaysia berkata kerjasama di Melaka hanya menguntungkan Bersatu manakala PH perlu mempertahankan kerjasama dengan parti di sebalik Langkah Sheraton.
"Kalau kita lihat kepada PRN di Johor dan PRN di Negeri Sembilan, mereka (Bersatu) tidak dapat meyakinkan bahawa mereka dapat membawa nilai tambahan kepada PH," katanya.
Lau berkata Bersatu mungkin mempunyai nilai tambah di Selangor kerana Azmin. Azmin adalah bekas menteri besar Selangor.
"Setakat mana Azmin dapat membawa nilai tambah kepada PH, yang itu masih tidak dapat ditentukan," katanya.

0700eac586b34b82: WASHINGTON: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Wednesday announced the creation of a new military command that would be dedicated to building and providing autonomous and robotic capabilities across the US military.

The command, which Hegseth said would be called "Autonomous Warfare Command," highlights the rapidly changing nature of warfare and the need to make progress on systems like drones and the use of artificial intelligence.

Creating a new command is not common — the last one was US Space Command in 2019 — and the move reflects the Pentagon's push to shift from costly conventional weapons platforms to cheaper, AI-driven autonomous systems that have proved decisive in recent conflicts.

Speaking in front of hundreds of ​junior officers and enlisted personnel at Quantico, Virginia, in a speech peppered with attacks on the media, Hegseth said the command would be led by a four-star officer.

"The pace of war is changing faster than the process to support it," Hegseth said in a speech called the "State of the Force," in which he announced other changes, including the creation of the office of religious affairs.
"Cheap compute, super intelligence, and advanced commercial manufacturing have enabled the proliferation of low-cost, high-precision strike," Hegseth added.
The US military currently has 11 combatant commands, which are responsible for different parts of the world and specific tasks.
Experts have expressed fears over the potential for unchecked AI development and technology rivalries that could further ​heighten risks across the global security environment.
Both China and ⁠the ​US — the two major drivers of cutting-edge AI development and its global adoption — have been at loggerheads over AI policies and ​industry practices.
Security experts from both countries have called for guardrails and consensus-building regarding AI in military systems, including nuclear weapons.
The United States has long relied on its vast military budget to field some of the world's most expensive weapons systems.
But there is an increasing realisation within the Pentagon that this is not sustainable.
"Today we need both quality and quantity," Hegseth said.
The technology of war has evolved rapidly in recent years, a shift starkly illustrated by Russia's war in Ukraine.
What began as a conflict dominated by tanks and artillery has increasingly become a drone war.
Outgunned in conventional armor and aircraft, Ukraine turned to inexpensive unmanned systems for reconnaissance and attack.
Drones are estimated to account for about 70 per cent of Russian casualties, enabling strikes to be carried out remotely and reducing the risk to pilots and aircrews.
The Pentagon has in recent years made some progress, including the creation of a task force — Joint Interagency Task Force 401 — that is focused on countering drones.
21a9c109d27d200f: KOTA KINABALU: The Health Ministry has called on medical officers appointed to Grade UD10 to report for duty immediately and complete the process at their respective Centres of Responsibility (PTj) by Oct 7.
In a statement today, the ministry said the appointments took effect on Sept 28, with officers offered placements through the ePlacement system.
"The reporting process for 4,255 medical officers appointed on a permanent basis under Phase 2/2026 is still ongoing," it said.

Malaysian Medical Association (MMA) president Dr L Sivanaesan previously said reports of a high number of medical officers failing to report for permanent postings in Sabah and Sarawak on Sept 28 should be taken seriously, particularly claims that some facilities received no new medical officers.
Previously, it was reported that the ministry planned to appoint 560 new permanent medical officers for Sabah from this month to help address the doctor shortage in the state.

Sabah MMA chairman Dr Brandon Patrick Senagang also said the majority of hospitals were losing medical officers, with only 47 of 138 medical officers from outside Sabah expected to report for hospital postings having done so when the figures were compiled.
"Based on information available to Sabah MMA involving hospital postings, 138 medical officers from outside Sabah were expected to report to hospitals across the state.
"But only 47 had reported for duty at the time the information was compiled — approximately 34 per cent," Brandon said in a separate statement.
The ministry urged all parties not to draw premature conclusions while the placement process was still underway.
"The process of medical officers reporting for duty at their respective placement facilities is still ongoing and has not yet been completed," it said.
cf8258b7c7412445: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — Six resolutions adopted at the Fifth National Research Conference on Governance, Integrity and Anti-Corruption (TIAR) 2026 last Friday will be submitted for consideration by the Special Cabinet Committee on National Governance (JKKTN) at its next meeting.

Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said this was to ensure the resolutions were translated into concrete improvements to the system, particularly efforts to strengthen corruption prevention, rather than remaining merely conference outcomes.

Speaking to reporters after the MACC’s 59th anniversary celebration and monthly assembly here today, he said one resolution called for the establishment of an integrated National Grant Governance Framework (KTGGN).

He said other resolutions included developing Government Procurement Regulations (Public-Private Partnerships) as specific regulations under the legal framework to strengthen the management of government concessions, as well as enhancing the eCOSS ecosystem through smart data integration to monitor cooking oil transactions.
Abd Halim said submitting the resolutions to the JKKTN was in line with MACC’s approach of strengthening corruption prevention through a more proactive, targeted and risk-based strategy.
In a related development, Abd Halim said the JKKTN, chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, meets three times a year.
He said the committee met today, but it could not table the six resolutions because the TIAR conference concluded only last Friday.
“So I think they may be tabled at the next meeting,” he said.
Meanwhile, Abd Halim said corruption prevention efforts should draw on investigation findings, data and risk analysis to identify areas that could create opportunities for corrupt practices.

He said Integrity Units should also be further empowered as strategic partners to management in addressing systemic weaknesses and identifying risks, so that breaches of regulations could be prevented at an early stage.

Earlier in his speech, Abd Halim said MACC’s efforts could not focus solely on action after an offence had been committed; prevention must instead be strengthened through an earlier, risk-based approach. — Bernama
84700ef666a31167: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's private healthcare market is projected to more than double to RM158 billion by 2029 from about RM74 billion in 2022.
This will be driven by an ageing population, rising chronic diseases and growing demand for private care, said Informa Markets, quoting Frost & Sullivan data.

Informa said the growth is expected to create wider opportunities for healthcare providers, medical device makers, pharmaceutical companies and other suppliers, as private hospital capacity and medical tourism continue to expand.
According to Frost & Sullivan, Malaysia's private healthcare market is set to grow from about RM74 billion in 2022 to RM158 billion by 2029, an 11.4 per cent compound annual growth rate.
Private hospital capacity is expected to reach about 23,500 beds by 2028, with investment flowing into areas including oncology, cardiology, day surgery, diagnostics, digital health and aged care.
Healthcare travel is adding to demand.
Malaysia Healthcare Travel Council data showed healthcare travel revenue reached RM3.35 billion in 2025, more than double pre-pandemic levels, with Indonesia accounting for 66 per cent.

The expansion is also reflected among listed healthcare operators, with IHH Healthcare, KPJ Healthcare and Sunway Healthcare reporting revenue growth of between 9 per cent and 21 per cent in their latest reported periods.

Against this backdrop, International Healthcare Week (IHW) 2027 will return to Kuala Lumpur from July 13-15 next year, bringing healthcare manufacturers, suppliers, buyers and investors together under one roof.
Organised by Informa with the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade) as strategic partner, the event will be held at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre.

IHW 2027 will bring together three exhibitions - CPHI South East Asia, World Health Expo (WHX) Kuala Lumpur and Medtec Southeast Asia - covering pharmaceuticals, medical devices, healthcare technology and hospital solutions.
Informa regional portfolio director for Asean Rungphech Chitanuwat said the event was intended to connect businesses across the region as Malaysia's healthcare market expands.
"Malaysia's healthcare market is rapidly growing fast, and the opportunity reaches well beyond its borders," she said.
"International Healthcare Week was created to support the growth of Southeast Asia's healthcare industry, and we are proud to bring it to Malaysia for the second time."
Matrade will help connect Malaysian healthcare companies, particularly micro, small and medium enterprises, with international buyers, investors and potential partners.
Matrade chief executive officer Dato' Indera Abu Bakar Yusof said healthcare was among Malaysia's promising export sectors.
"International Healthcare Week 2027 gives our exporters and MSMEs a direct platform to meet international buyers and form new partnerships," he said.
d0dab3e05d125796: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — A 22-year-old man has been charged with secretly filming four women while they were urinating in a toilet at a factory in Penang, as well as possessing obscene videos.

Berita Harian reported that Muhammad Mukhris Sulaiman pleaded not guilty to all five charges and claimed trial after they were read out before Magistrate Sharifah Razali at the Magistrate’s Court in Bukit Mertajam today.

For the first four charges, Muhammad Mukhris is accused of filming the women at a factory in Bukit Minyak, in the Central Seberang Perai district, between 11.44am and 6.55pm from September 2 to September 23.

The charges were brought under Section 509 of the Penal Code, which covers acts intended to insult a person’s modesty and carries a maximum penalty of five years’ imprisonment, a fine, or both upon conviction.
Muhammad Mukhris was also charged with possessing several obscene videos during an inspection at the Seberang Perai Tengah district police headquarters compound at 9.30am on September 24.
That charge was framed under Section 292 of the Penal Code, which provides for a jail term of up to three years, a fine, or both upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Siti Nur Amalina Harun appeared for the prosecution, while Muhammad Mukhris was represented by lawyer V Sivakumar.
The court granted him bail of RM15,000 for all five charges and ordered him not to approach the alleged victims until the conclusion of the trial.
The case is due to be mentioned again on November 19 for the submission of documents.
26c06d1807c4eda6: KUALA LUMPUR: Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) has completed a RM5.2 billion syndicated Islamic term financing exercise, one of the largest syndicated loan facilities arranged for an unlisted Malaysian company.
DNB said the financing comes as it prepares for the next phase of Malaysia's dual 5G network framework.
The financing is expected to support the planned exit of the Ministry of Finance Inc (MoF Inc) as an ordinary shareholder, it said today.

It will also facilitate the transition to equal ownership among DNB's mobile network operator (MNO) shareholders - CelcomDigi Bhd through Infranation Sdn Bhd, Maxis Broadband Sdn Bhd and YTL Power International Bhd - expected in early fourth quarter of this year.
MoF Inc will retain a special share in DNB to safeguard national interests and oversee key strategic matters.
The RM5.2 billion facility also refinances DNB's government guarantee revolving credit facility, which expired on Sept 29.
It provides the company with a long-term funding structure for its operations and network investments.
Maybank Investment Bank Bhd acted as mandated lead arranger, bookrunner and coordinating arranger.
AmInvestment Bank Bhd, CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd, RHB Islamic Bank Bhd and United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd were joint mandated lead arrangers.
AmInvestment Bank also acted as financial adviser to DNB.
The financing comes as DNB receives the full 100MHz of the 3.3GHz to 3.4GHz (F0) spectrum and converts its entire 240MHz spectrum holding to a spectrum assignment.
The assignment, issued by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission, takes effect today.
DNB said the expanded spectrum holding would increase network capacity, efficiency and performance, supporting faster speeds, lower latency and improved customer experience.
It would also enable the deployment of technologies such as Massive MIMO, carrier aggregation, 5G Advanced and artificial intelligence-driven network capabilities.

DNB chief executive officer Datuk Azman Ismail said the successful financing reflected confidence in the company's business fundamentals, operational track record and long-term role in Malaysia's digital economy.
"This financing provides DNB with a sustainable platform to operate on its own, continue investing in network enhancement and capacity expansion, and leverage our expanded spectrum assets," he said.
Azman said DNB remained committed to providing digital infrastructure as Malaysia moved towards a dual network framework.

"With strong financing, enhanced spectrum resources and a proven nationwide 5G platform, DNB is well positioned to support the government's AI Nation aspirations and help power Malaysia's next phase of digital growth," he said.
DNB said the financing and spectrum assignment would strengthen its ability to improve network quality and resilience, cater to future demand and support Malaysia's digital economy ambitions.

54421135cfbe9530: PETALING JAYA: Budget 2027 should shift industrial policy towards revitalising Malaysia’s "forgotten cities" rather than creating new economic centres from scratch, a policy think tank says.

Research for Social Advancement (Refsa) said pouring funds into greenfield mega-projects risked leaving behind established secondary towns that already possess productive infrastructure, skilled workers and local supply chains.

In a policy brief, the think tank said the Pre-Budget Statement 2027 recognised that resources for social development should be based on actual needs, and argued that the same approach should be applied to the economy.

Refsa said this principle should extend directly into industrial policy by leveraging existing regional assets such as underutilised factories, transport links and universities to drive the nation's next phase of growth.

"Often, forgotten cities are not places without economic foundations. Their problem is that these assets have often developed in fragments, become disconnected from one another, or have not been given a clear role in the country’s next phase of growth," Refsa said.

To unlock the economic potential of these areas, Refsa advocated a development framework that tailors strategies to each region’s strengths. It cited Johor as a clear example, with several distinct development models.

It pointed to Muar’s established industrial base spanning furniture, semiconductors and engineering, and recommended that the district deepen its technological capabilities to evolve into a knowledge-industrial city.

Similarly, Refsa suggested turning Kluang into the economic heart of central Johor by leveraging renewed railway connectivity to link manufacturing, logistics and cold-chain facilities with surrounding districts and ports.
Outside Johor, Refsa highlighted Ipoh and Taiping-Kamunting in Perak as prime examples of older industrial cities capable of adopting new economic functions while retaining their historical identity.
Refsa said such a framework did not require new mega-funds or added bureaucracy, but rather the coordination and convergence of existing federal, state and private sector resources.
a7eed6a9e2d2528b: PUTRAJAYA: Mahkamah Rayuan mengekalkan sabitan dan denda RM10,000 dikenakan terhadap aktivis Wong Yan Ke kerana menghina naib canselor Universiti Malaya (UM) ketika itu dan hadirin dengan melakukan protes pada majlis konvokesyen, pada 2019.

Panel tiga hakim dipengerusikan Hakim Noorin Badaruddin menolak rayuan Wong terhadap sabitan dan hukuman ke atasnya di bawah Seksyen 504 Kanun Keseksaan, yang sengaja mengaibkan dengan niat hendak membangkitkan pecah keamanan.
Mahkamah mendapati pertuduhan itu adalah sah selain pihak pendakwaan berjaya membuktikan semua elemen kesalahan melampaui keraguan munasabah, dan tidak wujud kegagalan sistem keadilan.
Hakim lain yang turut bersidang, Hakim Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz dan Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid.
Noorin, yang membacakan keputusan mahkamah, berkata tiada khilaf material oleh majistret dan tiada asas bagi Mahkamah Rayuan campur tangan dalam keputusan Mahkamah Tinggi.
"Kami sebulat suara berpuas hati bahawa rayuan perayu terhadap sabitan dan hukuman tidak mempunyai merit. Rayuan ini ditolak," katanya.
Panel hakim mengekalkan hukuman dijatuhkan Mahkamah Tinggi pada 15 April 2025 – denda RM10,000, atau penjara enam bulan jika gagal membayar denda. Wong, 29, telah pun menjelaskan denda berkenaan.
Ketika bercakap kepada Wong, Noorin menegaskan mahkamah bukannya menghukumnya kerana berpegang pandangan berbeza.
"Mahkamah tidak menghukum anda kerana mempunyai pandangan berbeza. Mahkamah menghukum tingkah laku yang mengikut dapatan mahkamah melampaui had ditetapkan undang-undang," katanya.
Beliau berkata, kebebasan bersuara merupakan hak yang penting, namun tidak memberi hak kepada seseorang untuk membelakangi undang-undang.
"Dalam masyarakat demokratik, kita bukan sahaja perlu mendaulatkan hak bersuara, tetapi juga menerima tanggungjawab yang hadir bersama hak tersebut," katanya.
Noorin berkata, Wong kekal bebas bersuara, mengkritik, dan tidak bersetuju, namun perlu melaksanakan kebebasan itu dalam cara menghormati undang-undang.

Pada Oktober 2023, Mahkamah Majistret Kuala Lumpur mendapati Wong bersalah kerana menghina naib canselor UM ketika itu, Abdul Rahim Hashim dan hadirin lain dengan membawa sepanduk ke atas pentas menuntut peletakan jawatan Rahim, semasa majlis konvokesyen 14 Okt 2019.

Majistret menolak hujahnya bahawa beliau tidak mempunyai saluran lain menyuarakan pandangannya, sambil menyatakan terdapat pelbagai platform lain boleh digunakannya sebelum bertindak mengadakan tunjuk perasaan itu.
Mahkamah Tinggi menolak rayuan Wong terhadap sabitannya dan mengenakan tambahan denda RM5,000, menjadikan jumlah keseluruhan RM10,000.

Peguam Haijan Omar, Farida Mohammad, Chan Yen Hui, Asyraaf Abu Bakar Hamzah, dan Chong Kar Yan mewakili Wong, manakala Timbalan Pendakwa Raya Jasmee Hameeza Jaafar dan Zain Ibrahim bertindak bagi pihak pendakwaan.
fb4e90919c9caca2: SHAH ALAM: A food delivery rider caught on a viral video knocking down a schoolgirl at a pedestrian crossing was charged at the magistrate's court here today with riding without due care and attention.
Muhammad Haziq Izzuddin Ruslan, 25, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read out before magistrate Muhammad Syafiq Sulaiman.
He was charged with riding a Yamaha motorcycle on a road without due care and attention to other road users, resulting in a collision with a pedestrian.
The offence was allegedly committed at Persiaran Saujana 4, Sungai Buloh, at 12.08pm on Sept 28.
He was charged under Section 43(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, which provides for a fine of between RM5,000 and RM10,000 and a jail term of up to 12 months upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Alia Anisa Khairus Masnan sought RM5,000 bail with one surety.
Lawyer Muhamad Saifullah Muhamad Azmi, representing Haziq, however, urged the court to reduce the bail, saying his client had no fixed income and was supporting his unemployed parents.
"My client is single and his family has prepared RM2,000 for bail. His younger brother is present as his surety and will ensure his attendance at future court proceedings," he said.
Syafiq allowed Haziq bail at RM2,000 with one surety and ordered him to report to a police station once a month.
The court fixed Nov 12 for mention.
Haziq, who had been released on police bail, appeared in court on his own and was seen walking with a limp due to injuries sustained in the accident.
Outside the courtroom, Saifullah said his client claimed he did not notice the girl crossing the road as parked cars on both sides had obstructed his view.
"He told me he did not notice the girl crossing.
"She suddenly appeared in front of him and he could not control his motorcycle or avoid her," he said.
Saifullah said Haziq also denied riding recklessly and had stopped to check on the girl after the collision.
A video of the incident went viral showing the schoolgirl crossing at a pedestrian crossing before being hit by a motorcycle.
The impact sent the girl flying, while Haziq lost control of his motorcycle and fell onto the road.
41fbed98f46fa8b8: NAGOYA: Abdul Samad smashed 22 off five balls in an unbeaten 30 on Thursday as Pakistan's men cruised into their maiden Asian Games cricket final, where arch-rivals India are the potential opponents.
Pakistan thumped Bangladesh by six wickets with nine balls to spare in a semi-final reduced to 13 overs because the outfield was too wet for play at the start time of 9:00 am.
They will face either world champions India or Sri Lanka, who clash later, for the gold medal on Saturday.
"To be honest, we don't really care about who will win and who will reach the final," said Pakistan batsman Saim Ayub, who scored 21.
"All we care about is winning the final, no matter who we are playing against."
Pakistan asked Bangladesh to bat on a heavily cracked pitch that had been covered for almost a week at the Korogi Athletic Park Stadium because of torrential rain.
Under clear blue skies, Pakistan's bowlers then had Bangladesh reeling at 21-3 and then 45-4 in the sixth over.
Towhid Hridoy led a recovery with 42 off 25 balls with two fours and four sixes as Bangladesh posted 111-7.
Pakistan lost three early wickets as they chased quick runs.
But once Samad and Hasan Nawaz came together at 53-4 in the seventh over the result never looked in doubt.
The pair posted an unbroken stand of 59 in 32 balls as they raced to their target.
Samad was 30 not out at the end off 15 balls while Nawaz was on 27 at the end.
The match was effectively decided by Samad's remarkable 22 runs off five balls in the 10th over, bowled by Bangladesh's Mustafizur Rahman, when Pakistan still needed 36 from 24 balls.
Nawaz prodded a single off to third man off the first ball before Samad launched a towering six over long on and four fours off consecutive deliveries to leave Pakistan needing only 13 from 18 balls.
Bangladesh will play the loser of the other semi-final for the bronze medal, also on Saturday.-AFP
cf1d703d3ed5b564: JAKARTA: An Indonesian police spokesperson said on Thursday that the captain of a ship that capsized in the Java Sea last month has been arrested and will face criminal charges for his role in an accident that killed at least 78 people.
The Virgo Transport 8 ferry was carrying 243 people when it capsized in bad weather in the Java Sea on Sept 13 during a voyage from Surabaya in East Java to Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan.
Divers have been circling the ship, battling against fast sea currents and the ship's unstable structure, to search for those missing on deck.
National police spokesperson Trunoyudo Wisnu Andiko said that the ship's captain has been arrested and named a criminal suspect.

Senior police official Kukuh Prabowo was quoted by state news agency Antara as saying on Wednesday that the captain was suspected of violating Indonesia's shipping law by knowingly sailing an unseaworthy vessel, an offence punishable by up to 10 years in prison when it causes deaths and property damage.
Neither Wisnu nor Kukuh provided any details of the alleged crimes.
The current death toll from the incident is 78 people, while 57 people remain missing, Indonesia's search and rescue agency said late on Wednesday.

56998c7870818c2e: BUKIT MERTAJAM: A 22-year-old man was charged in the magistrate's court here today with five counts of recording four women urinating in a toilet and possessing obscene videos.

7e22c270529d9c92: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — More than 268,000 taxpayers have submitted 1.99 billion e-invoices as of October 1, the Inland Revenue Board (IRB) said.
Its chief executive officer Datuk Abu Tariq Jamaluddin said 196,031 taxpayers accounted for submissions under phase four of the e-invoicing rollout.
“The implementation of e-invoicing is being carried out in stages, with the government recently announcing an increase in the exemption threshold from RM1 million to RM3 million.

“This benefits micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), as businesses with annual turnover below RM3 million are no longer required to implement e-invoicing,” he told reporters after officiating the launch of ‘Bulan HASiL 2026’.
The revised threshold, which took effect on September 1, 2026, exempts MSMEs with annual income or sales of less than RM3 million from the e-invoicing requirement.
Abu Tariq said 5,582 taxpayers had submitted e-invoices under phase one, followed by 14,579 under phase two and 51,815 under phase three.
The e-invoicing system was introduced on August 1, 2024.
Meanwhile, he said IRB had more than 620,000 active corporate tax files and over 7.6 million active individual tax files as of August 31, 2026.
In his speech, Abu Tariq said Bulan HASiL, held under the theme “Voluntary Disclosure, Shared Responsibility”, provided taxpayers with an opportunity to return to voluntary tax compliance.

He said IRB had introduced several special initiatives, including the Special Voluntary Disclosure programme (PKPS) covering e-invoicing and stamp duty, as well as the Voluntary Income Tax Disclosure campaign.

“In brief, the PKPS e-Invois focuses on e-invoicing compliance, while the PKPS Duti Setem allows taxpayers to regularise their stamp duty matters with the benefit of penalty exemptions. The Voluntary Income Tax Disclosure campaign, meanwhile, provides an opportunity to correct income declarations,” he added.
One of the key activities under Bulan HASiL is the tax literacy roadshow, which is being held nationwide throughout October 2026. — Bernama
8116fcc59047f5f6: AICHI: Judoka Amir Daniel Abdul Majeed came within one second of pulling off a stunning upset on his Asian Games debut when he faced former world runner-up Sotaro Fujiwara of Japan.

In the round-of-16 bout in the men's under-81kg category at the Aichi International Arena today, Amir was on the verge of victory after pinning Fujiwara for 19 seconds, only for the Japanese judoka to break free just before the required 20 seconds for an ippon.
Fujiwara then threw Amir to score an ippon and end the Malaysian's challenge, denying him a place in the quarter-finals.
Amir, 21, admitted that a last-second tactical shift proved costly, but said the experience would serve as a crucial lesson in his career.
"I only needed one more second to secure the win. I managed to hold him down for 19 seconds, and to win outright I had to hold on for 20 seconds.
"After that, my tactical shift wasn't quite right, and that was my fault. I need to learn from this expensive mistake and carry these lessons forward into my Olympic dream," he said.
Amir admitted he was nervous competing at his first Asian Games and in Japan, the birthplace of judo.
"I was definitely very nervous because it's my first appearance, and my opponent was a former world runner-up as well as a World Tour medallist.
"However, anything can happen in judo, and I just tried to give my best," he said.
Amir, a final-year student at Universiti Sains Malaysia, said competing at the Asian Games had given him a clearer picture of the level he must reach in his pursuit of an Olympic berth.
"Judo at the Asian Games is like a mini Olympics because all the top athletes are here, including Olympic champions and medallists.
"I learned that experience is extremely vital, and I need to place greater trust in my own capabilities," he added.
In July, Amir made history by becoming the first Malaysian judoka to win a Commonwealth Games gold medal in Glasgow.
368f2af52d3b94e0: PETALING JAYA, Oct 1 — Mercedes will roll out a striking new look at this weekend’s Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, with the W17 set to carry a special Petronas inspired livery.

a90489c80eea5448: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian-German Chamber of Commerce and Industry (MGCC) is hosting a five-day delegation of seven German waste management and recycling technology providers in Malaysia.

The programme, held from Sept 28 to Oct 2, aims to give Malaysian businesses direct access to German solutions in waste collection, sorting, recycling and material recovery, while supporting Malaysia's transition from a landfill-dependent system towards a more regulated, technology-driven circular economy.
In a statement on Wednesday, MGCC executive director Hannes Farlock said Malaysia had set a clear direction to reduce the amount of waste sent to landfills and recover more value from waste.
"Getting there takes more than policy; it takes the right technology, adapted to local conditions, and backed by partners committed for the long term.

"German companies bring decades of experience in exactly that. Through this delegation, we want Malaysian businesses and authorities to meet these solution providers face to face, test ideas against real needs and build partnerships that last well beyond this week," he said.

MGCC said the programme features a conference and business networking session, where the German companies will present their technologies to an expected audience of about 100 participants from Malaysia's public and private sectors, followed by individually arranged business-to-business (B2B) meetings matched to each participant's business objectives.
It said the delegation comprises Eggersmann GmbH, Flottweg SE, Naue GmbH & Co. KG, Recco Deutschland GmbH, Tholander Ablufttechnik GmbH, Tomra Sorting GmbH and Westeria Fördertechnik GmbH.

"Their expertise spans mobile shredding and screening machinery, mechanical separation technology, geosynthetics for environmental and infrastructure engineering, non-ferrous metal recovery from incinerator bottom ash, exhaust air purification, sensor-based sorting, and recycling and material handling equipment," it said.

The delegation will also meet key public-sector stakeholders, including the National Solid Waste Management Department, the Solid Waste Management and Public Cleansing Corporation, URBANICE Malaysia and Subang Jaya City Council.

The business initiation trip is organised by MGCC in cooperation with SBS systems for business solutions GmbH, on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy, as part of its Market Development Programme for small and medium enterprises and Export Initiative Environmental Technologies.
e4f3cd9b09034079: SHAH ALAM: Seorang penghantar makanan yang sebelum ini tular dalam video kerana melanggar seorang pelajar di lintasan pejalan kaki, mengaku tidak bersalah di Mahkamah Majistret atas pertuduhan memandu secara tidak cermat.

Terdahulu, Timbalan Pendakwa Raya Alia Anisa Khairus Masnan mencadangkan tertuduh dibenarkan diikat jamin RM5,000 dengan seorang penjamin.

Mahkamah kemudian membenarkan tertuduh diikat jamin sebanyak RM2,000 dengan seorang penjamin serta syarat tambahan melaporkan diri di balai polis sebulan sekali selain menetapkan sebutan semula kes pada 12 Nov depan.
Isnin lepas, video yang tular memaparkan seorang pelajar yang baru keluar daripada sebuah kenderaan dilanggar penunggang motosikal ketika sedang melintas di lintasan berkenaan.

62afc017883b88fe: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek has ordered the immediate suspension of all programmes involving freelance speakers in schools following allegations circulating on social media involving a freelance speaker who had previously conducted programmes with pupils.

0a2ef7aa7298c896: PUTRAJAYA: Ketua Pengarah Agensi Kawalan dan Perlindungan Sempadan (AKPS) Shuhaily Mohd Zain mendakwa terdapat usaha mencemarkan imej agensi itu dan dirinya susulan video insiden di Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa Kuala Lumpur (KLIA) yang tular.

384d0a3b9331707d: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has been urged to recognise marine food security and marine pollution prevention as a matter of national resilience and economic priority in the 2027 Budget.

Hexagon Synergy Group sustainability and strategic planning head, Dr Nur Zulaikha Yusof, said the 2027 financial blueprint should support greater investment in the infrastructure and systems needed to prevent marine pollution at source.
She cautioned that failing to address this issue could harm the ecosystems that sustain fisheries and aquaculture.
"These sectors are vital to the nation's economy, valued at over RM1.3 billion, providing employment for more than 100,000 people and serving as a crucial source of income for many communities.

"Crucially, this includes deploying robust port reception facilities (PRFs) for the proper collection, treatment and disposal of ship-generated waste," the expert in waste management and environmental sustainability told Bernama today.
PRFs are specialised facilities in ports designed to receive, manage, and process waste generated by ships, ensuring compliance with international maritime environmental regulations.

The government in its development and financial plans should place greater emphasis on protecting Malaysia's marine environment as a core component of the nation's environmental, social, and governance (ESG) agenda.

This is particularly so as Malaysia seeks to strengthen marine food security, safeguard coastal livelihoods and expand its wider blue economy, which entails the sustainable use of ocean and coastal resources.

Nur Zulaikha said ships generate oily residues, sewage, plastics, garbage and other operational waste which, if not properly managed, could enter the marine environment, placing further pressure on coastal waters and habitats, damaging ecosystems that support fisheries and increasing clean-up costs.

The consequences extend beyond the environment, as the health of marine ecosystems is closely linked to seafood availability, fishing activities and the livelihoods of coastal communities, underscoring the need for Budget 2027 to prioritise investment in measures that strengthen marine protection and, in turn, safeguard the country's food security and coastal economy.

"The warning is already visible in Malaysia's fisheries catch, which, despite a brief recovery in 2022, Southeast Asian Fisheries Development Centre (SEAFDEC) data show marine capture production shrinking by nearly 190,000 tonnes between 2019 and 2023, from about 1.46 million to 1.27 million tonnes.
"For a sector that feeds the nation and sustains coastal economies, the direction matters as much as the number," she said.

Nur Zulaikha emphasised that marine food security should not just be evaluated at the landing jetty. It also encompasses the availability and safety of seafood, the accessibility of fishing grounds for coastal communities, and the sustainability of livelihoods in fishing, aquaculture, processing, and trade.

Protecting the sea from avoidable pollution is therefore not only an environmental obligation but also an ESG imperative, as the health of marine ecosystems underpins both food security and coastal economic activity.
"PRFs effectively translate this priority into action by safely managing ship waste onshore and protecting Malaysia's seas, food security, and coastal livelihoods," she said.

Nur Zulaikha said PRFs will not rebuild fish stocks, nor could they replace effective fisheries management, habitat protection, climate adaptation, sustainable fishing or controls on pollution from land. Their role is narrower, but the impact is tangible.

By providing vessels with a controlled and reliable means of transferring waste ashore, PRFs could reduce the risks of contamination, habitat damage, disruption to fishing and deterioration of waters that sustain seafood production.
EFFECTIVE PRF SYSTEM REQUIRES CLEAR RULES, ENFORCEMENT

She also implored the government to consider establishing a dedicated PRF policy and regulatory framework to provide a clear legal basis for waste delivery, cost-recovery arrangements, monitoring and enforcement, drawing on European best practices for PRFs.
"The European Union's approach under Directive (EU) 2019/883 on port reception facilities for the delivery of waste from ships provides a useful international benchmark for an effective PRF system.

"It recognises that preventing waste discharges at sea requires more than physical infrastructure; it must be reinforced by clear waste-delivery obligations, appropriate cost-recovery arrangements, effective monitoring and consistent enforcement," she said.
Nur Zulaikha said evidence from earlier REFIT Evaluations of the PRF Directive supports this broader approach.
The amount of garbage delivered by vessels to EU ports increased substantially, with deliveries in 2013 reported to be more than double those recorded in 2004.

Over the same period, potential oil-spill detections declined from an average of 10.77 per 1,000 square kilometres in 2008 to 3.89 in 2013, indicating a corresponding reduction in estimated oily-waste discharges at sea.
PRFS DRIVING MALAYSIA'S ESG AGENDA
Nur Zulaikha said well-functioning PRFs could directly support Malaysia's ESG agenda by turning environmental responsibility into a controlled, measurable waste-management system.

For Malaysia, strengthening PRFs is not simply about meeting international obligations; it is about protecting the marine environment, preserving resources that sustain food security and delivering stronger ESG outcomes.

By keeping ship-generated waste out of the marine environment, protecting coastal resources and livelihoods, and ensuring waste is documented, traceable, and managed through authorised channels, PRFs bring environmental protection, social resilience, and governance accountability into a single operational framework.

"In this way, PRFs can help ports and maritime stakeholders demonstrate tangible ESG performance while supporting Malaysia's broader ambition for a cleaner, more responsible and resilient maritime economy," she said.

0922ed9192d7f06e: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain said he was prepared to accept any action taken by the government over a viral video from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), saying he would take responsibility for what happened.

de07dedf57f8c504: BANGKOK: German chipmaker Infineon Technologies opened a new facility in Thailand on Thursday, as Southeast Asia's second-largest economy pushes to attract investment into the semiconductor industry amid rising regional competition.

0efd88c0601dd994: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today upheld the conviction and RM10,000 fine imposed on activist Wong Yan Ke for insulting the then Universiti Malaya vice-chancellor and convocation attendees during a protest in 2019.

A three-member bench chaired by Justice Noorin Badaruddin dismissed Wong’s appeal against his conviction and sentence under Section 504 of the Penal Code, which criminalises intentional insult with the intent to provoke a breach of the peace.
The court found that the charge was valid, the prosecution proved all elements of the offence beyond reasonable doubt, and there was no miscarriage of justice.
The other judges on the bench were Justices Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz and Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid.
Noorin, who delivered the court’s decision, said there was no material misdirection by the magistrate and no basis for the appellate court to interfere with the High Court’s decision.
"We are unanimously satisfied that the appellant’s appeal against conviction and sentence is without merit. The appeal is dismissed," she said.
The bench maintained the sentence imposed by the High Court on April 15 last year – a RM10,000 fine, in default of six months’ jail. Wong, 29, paid the fine.
Addressing Wong directly, Noorin said the court was not punishing him for holding a different view.
"The court does not punish you for holding a different view. It punishes conduct which, in the court’s finding, has exceeded the limits prescribed by law," she said.
She said freedom of speech was an important right but did not give a person the right to disregard the law.
"In a democratic society, we must not only uphold the right to speak, but also accept the responsibilities that come with that right," she said.
Noorin said Wong remained free to speak, criticise and disagree, but should exercise that freedom in a manner that respects the law.

In October 2023, the Kuala Lumpur magistrates’ court convicted Wong of insulting then UM vice-chancellor Abdul Rahim Hashim and other attendees by carrying a placard on stage demanding Rahim’s resignation during a convocation ceremony on Oct 14, 2019.
The magistrate rejected his argument that he had no other means of expressing his views, saying there were various avenues he could have used before resorting to the protest.
The High Court dismissed Wong’s appeal against his conviction and imposed a further RM5,000 fine, bringing the total to RM10,000.

Lawyers Haijan Omar, Farida Mohammad, Chan Yen Hui, Asyraaf Abu Bakar Hamzah and Chong Kar Yan appeared for Wong, while deputy public prosecutors Jasmee Hameeza Jaafar and Zain Ibrahim represented the prosecution.
f01e8f810ddb2a45: LETTER: It's been 10 years since the landmark 2016 South China Sea Arbitral Award between the Philippines and China. The argument remains on who actually won the legal argument.
The more consequential question is what does the dispute means for future maritime order in the region.
The Arbitral Award clarified an important provision in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), including questions pertaining to historical rights and maritime entitlements.
With respect to matters addressed by the Tribunal, the Award remains final and legally binding between the Philippines and China.

A decade has past, even so tensions remain persistent. In addition, the situation surrounding the South China Sea has evolved from competing maritime claims to a broader competition over law, power and strategic narratives.

The anniversary of the Award illustrated this division. Fourteen countries have reaffirmed the Award and reiterated the importance of UNCLOS while Beijing reiterated that the award is "illegal, null and void".

China has also continued to advocate its alternative legal interpretation, through its 2024 report titled 'Refuting the South China Sea Arbitration Award Again'. These positions demonstrate the continuing gap between competing conceptions of maritime governance.
It is now evidence that there are three interconnected contests. First is the contest of law, involving the competing interpretations of UNCLOS, historical rights and international jurisprudence.

Second is power, that is increasingly characterised by the presence of Coast Guard, military militia and naval activities below the threshold of armed conflict. This grey-zone situation or tactic employed makes deterrence and crisis management all the more important.

Third is contest of narratives through legal reports, diplomatic statements, academic publication and social media can now be seen influencing how governments and societies understand legitimate maritime behaviour.

For Malaysia, the current situation presents a complex strategic challenge. As a maritime trading nation, Asean member and claimant state, it has direct interest in a South China Sea that is peaceful, stable and open.
In concurrent, Malaysia maintains constructive economic, diplomatic and security relationship with its strategic partners such as China, the United States, Japan and Australia.

It should not be viewed as simply hedging because for Malaysia, strategic autonomy means preserving the policy space necessary to protect its national interests while maintaining constructive relations with all major powers.

However, strategic autonomy requires resilience. Malaysia must continue to strengthen its maritime security, inter-agency coordination and ability to respond proportionately against grey-zone tactics.
It also needs to increase resilience against information operations and competing narratives that could affect public understanding and national decision making.

For Malaysia, Asean remains essential and the way forward is clear that is to uphold international law, strengthening strategic resilience, reinforce Asean centrality as well as maintain constructive engagement with all major power.
Therefore, the South China Sea is ultimately a test not just in maritime security, but whether the region can preserve its stability, openness and cooperation upon which its prosperity depends on.
VICE ADMIRAL DATUK YUSNE MOKHTAR
Malaysian Institute of Defence and Security (MiDAS)
Kuala Lumpur

5ed3c3c71bb68dca: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Haze from Indonesian wildfires has blanketed neighbouring Malaysia and Singapore for more than a month, closing schools and sending respiratory complaints skyrocketing.
It is not the first time Indonesian haze has caused a regional pollution crisis, but neighbouring countries have few options for legal recourse, experts say:
Case at the ICJ
Suggestions that Malaysia and Singapore take Indonesia to the UN’s highest judicial organ, the International Court of Justice in The Hague, face a basic obstacle:
“The main issue is jurisdiction, as the ICJ generally requires the consent of both states,” said Professor Mohd Hazmi Mohd Rusli of Universiti Sains Islam Malaysia.

The ICJ can only hear a dispute where states have accepted its jurisdiction, for example through a special agreement, compatible declarations recognising the court’s compulsory jurisdiction, or a treaty clause referring disputes to it.

Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore are neither signatories nor parties to the 1979 Convention on Long-range Transboundary Air Pollution, a European-centred treaty framework intended to curb cross-border air pollution.
And experts agree Indonesia would be unlikely to willingly accept ICJ jurisdiction on the issue.
All three countries are parties to the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution, but the 2002 deal has no clause on litigation before the ICJ.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The city skyline is shrouded in haze in Kuala Lumpur on September 15, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
What about Asean?
The Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution is a legally binding regional treaty, intended to prevent and monitor cross-border haze from land and forest fires, and to mitigate its effects.
But its enforcement provisions are limited.
“It is legally binding, but it does not provide a mechanism for one member state to simply sue another,” said Hazmi.
Instead, it seeks to solve the problem through “national action and regional cooperation”.

Legal analysts say Asean’s emphasis on consensus, sovereignty and non-interference puts the brakes on how much diplomatic pressure can be applied to member states over domestic land management and fire enforcement.

“For now, I think the more practical approach is stronger Asean cooperation, including hotspot monitoring, information sharing, prevention and stronger enforcement against illegal burning,” Hazmi said.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Haze envelopes the administrative capital of Putrajaya on September 18, 2026. — Bernama pic
Civil action
One option could be for Malaysians or Singaporeans to try to sue companies linked to the fires in an Indonesian court, said Azam Hawari, a legal expert at the environmental law charity, ClientEarth.

However, “claimants would need to show a link between the company’s activities, the haze that reached them, and their losses,” Azam said, adding he was not aware of such a case having been brought successfully.
Added Hazmi: “Transboundary haze does not automatically mean Indonesia is internationally responsible.”
“There must still be sufficient evidence to establish the link between activities in Indonesia and the harm suffered in Malaysia or Singapore,” he said.
Previous attempts
Singapore enacted its own Transboundary haze Pollution Act in 2014, after pollution levels spiked into hazardous territory the year before, followed by another episode in 2015.
The law aimed to punish companies whose activities outside Singapore caused or contributed to unhealthy levels of haze in Singapore.
Enforcement proved a major weakness because it relied heavily on cooperation from foreign authorities.
Establishing responsibility was also challenging because it required authorities to share maps pinpointing fire hotspots, and conflicting or overlapping land rights could further complicate matters.
Bringing a case against some companies with no presence in Singapore also made collecting fines or damages hard.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
People stand on the observation deck of the Marina Bay Sands on a hazy day in Singapore September 28, 2026. — AFP pic
Singapore’s investigations into four Indonesian companies over their alleged role in the 2015 transboundary haze remain open and proved a source of diplomatic tensions with Jakarta at the time.

Singapore will now most likely “wait for Indonesia to finger certain companies first before we take action against these same companies under the Act”, said Professor Alan Tan, an environmental law expert at the National University of Singapore.
“Otherwise, any action that Singapore takes would appear to the Indonesians to be unilateral, and could be politically controversial.”
Tan said: “Regrettably, not much has changed by way of how the root causes of fires remain unaddressed in Indonesia.” — AFP

The defence secretary also addressed autonomous warfare, meaning the use of weapons systems and artificial intelligence capable of operating and carrying out attacks without direct human intervention.

The Pentagon expects the project to produce its findings within 120 days.

2eb758ca843ac226: LONDON: The UK government is facing mounting pressure to end a £330-million contract between the National Health Service and AI giant Palantir, as doctors, lawmakers and campaigners warn of ethical risks.

The US company, co-founded by billionaire Peter Thiel – a close ally of US President Donald Trump – has enjoyed a growing role in Britain's public sector and the contract, awarded in 2023, allows it to provide a data management platform to the NHS.

Worth around US$440 million, the Federated Data Platform (FDP) is designed to improve coordination between hospitals and help manage and streamline appointments, making more efficient use of resources.
The NHS insists sensitive patient data remains stored in Britain, is not owned by Palantir and is not used for commercial purposes or AI training.

But critics point to the firm's broader work, including with the Israeli military and US immigration authorities, arguing such activities undermine any technological benefits as well as trust in the health service.

"The NHS has to function on trust – the trust I can tell my doctor anything. Those ethical concerns are basically poisoning everything," Duncan McCann, head of technology and data at the campaign group Good Law Project, told AFP.
Medical organisations and rights activists are planning protests on Thursday outside some 30 hospitals as well as Palantir's London headquarters.
They are urging the government to use a break clause that would prevent the contract being renewed beyond March 2027.
So far new Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who took office in July, has not publicly commented on the contract, which is under review with ministers expected to decide by December.
The British Medical Association (BMA) has urged doctors not to use the platform, citing risks to patient trust, data security and NHS independence.

"Given Palantir's track record, including controversies in the US involving immigration enforcement... we believe there must be a complete break from Palantir technologies in the NHS," BMA chair Tom Dolphin told the British Medical Journal in February.
A YouGov poll published in July found 65 per cent of Britons backed ending the contract.
But supporters argue the system is delivering results and around two-thirds of NHS hospitals have adopted the platform.
Palantir, which did not respond to AFP requests for a comment, says it has helped enable 110,000 additional operations while reducing waiting lists.

"The benefits of the FDP service are clear, with thousands more patients benefitting every month, including through the reduction in the number of unnecessary days spent in hospital after treatment," a Department of Health spokesperson told AFP.
The debate has widened beyond healthcare.

A parliamentary committee recently warned of growing UK dependence on US technology providers, and one of its members, Liberal Democrat MP Martin Wrigley, has called for a "sovereign" British alternative.
"That has to be within the control of a UK, preferably UK-owned firm, but certainly a UK firm that understands the ethics and way that the NHS works," he told AFP.

He warned of the risks that Trump could arbitrarily decide that Palantir's services to the UK could be "switched off" if for instance "he doesn't like what Andy Burnham says, or they differ on Ukraine or something."
Palantir has secured multiple public sector contracts in Britain, including a £240-million defence deal signed in 2025.
The UK is now Palantir's second-largest global market, accounting for 10 percent of the company's revenue in 2025.
France however this year decided to move away from using Palantir's software in their intelligence agencies, replacing it with software developed by French company ChapsVision.
German media reported that Berlin has acquired the French technology and is testing it.
London Mayor Sadiq Khan also blocked a £50-million contract between the Metropolitan Police and Palantir in May, citing procurement concerns, prompting the company to launch legal action.
Several British organisations have also chosen to part ways with the firm.

In northern England, NHS Greater Manchester, which manages the region's hospitals and local healthcare providers, has spent the past decade building its own data platform capable of performing some of the same functions as the FDP.
"What we've built to meet the system needs is better" for local patients, the provider's chief data officer, Matt Hennessey, told AFP, adding other regions could also achieve the same results.

f603ef5266417692: BRASÍLIA, Oct 1 — A Brazilian judge on Wednesday ordered the messaging platform Discord to do more to protect underage users after detecting shortfalls that allegedly led to the suicide of a 13-year-old girl.
The South American nation is one of the most active online regulators on the planet and last month sued Discord for nearly US$100 million after the teenager’s death in July.
Wednesday’s ruling ordered the platform to strengthen its parental control and age verification mechanisms, among other measures.
Failure to comply with these “emergency” provisions will result in a daily fine of around US$20,000, the ruling said.
The court in Brasilia has not yet ruled on the lawsuit filed by the government over Discord’s alleged failure to protect children from harmful content.
During a 45-minute livestream, other teenage users allegedly encouraged a young girl to kill an animal, and when she failed to do so, goaded her into killing herself.
Brazil’s National Data Protection Agency (ANPD) ordered Discord to suspend livestreams following the suicide in a small town in the centre-west of the country.
That same month, the platform introduced a plan to improve its safety features, but the measures were deemed insufficient by Brazilian authorities.
The US-based company with over 90 million active daily users worldwide did not immediately respond to an AFP request for comment on the latest ruling.
Brazil this year made it compulsory for platforms to link under-16 accounts to those of their parents and to verify users’ ages. — AFP
5497e112a5cd5d06: PETALING JAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has denied serving an asset declaration notice on the 12-year-old son of former human resources minister M Saravanan.

"Under the law, there is no specific age category stated, whether a person is an adult or a child. What is stated is in relation to relatives or associates.
"So, in the case of the 12-year-old, we exercised our discretion and considered what was reasonable. We decided not to serve a notice on his 12-year-old son," Harian Metro quoted him as saying.
Halim said MACC previously issued notices to Saravanan, his wife and his children, although some family members were unable to appear as they were overseas.
He said the 12-year-old’s presence at the MACC headquarters did not mean he was there to receive a notice related to the investigation.
"The child was not physically present to receive a notice. He was merely accompanying his parents," he said.
Former minister P Waytha Moorthy previously accused MACC of abusing its powers by allegedly requiring Saravanan’s 12-year-old son to appear at its headquarters to receive the notice.
Saravanan and members of his family went to the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya on Monday to receive notices requiring them to declare their assets.
Saravanan had questioned MACC’s decision to summon his 12-year-old son, arguing that the notice could have been served through him as the child’s parent.
The notices were issued as part of MACC’s investigation into Saravanan over alleged corruption involving the approval of foreign worker quotas.

3d483ad58d55328f: PARIS, Oct 1 — French security forces on Wednesday detained over 600 people while dozens of police and gendarmes were wounded as protests that have seen blockades of high schools and violent clashes escalated, the interior minister said.
The movement in the lycées, attended by students aged 15 to 18 for their final three years of secondary education in France, has angered the government.

Eighty-three police officers and gendarmes were wounded on Wednesday during the protests, which affected a total of 356 schools, he added.
The minister slammed the “targeting of law enforcement officers, the throwing of projectiles, acts of violence, verbal abuse, attempted arson, and what amounts... to urban violence.”
Since the start of the unrest last week, 119 students and staff members have been injured, Education Minister Edouard Geffray said.

The cites worst affected Wednesday included Paris, Bordeaux in the southwest and Lyon in the southeast, and the northern city of Lille where police again used tear gas in clashes, AFP correspondents said.
“It is imperative that our students be able to return to class — especially those who are currently prevented from doing so,” Geffray said.
Speaking in Madrid, President Emmanuel Macron slammed hard-left politicians he accused of “legitimising violence” in the French school protests.

“We don’t condone vandalism; we came to defend our rights because we have horrendous schedules — we work 8.00am to 6.00pm and that’s not right,” Juan, from the Montbello high school in the northern city of Lille which had been blockaded over the last days, told AFP. — AFP
